title: Regression suite for function-call JSON stability under FP8/INT8 profiles
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: build a deterministic regression and CI gating suite that verifies structured output (function-call JSON) correctness when models are served using FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles. We will measure schema-adherence regressions relative to a FP32 baseline, triage patterns of failures, and iterate on calibration and runtime safeguards (fallbacks, adjusted quant profiles).

Scope:
- Create a curated prompt corpus exercising function-calling shapes: nested objects, optional fields, arrays, polymorphic types, long string fields, edge-case numeric ranges, empty arrays/objects, and streaming split tokens.
- Design calibration runs for FP8 variants (e4m3, e5m2) and INT8 profiles used in production; capture calibration checkpoints and quant stats.
- Implement automated JSON-schema validation (ajv + python-jsonschema) and a lightweight semantic comparator for tolerate-able ordering/whitespace differences.
- Define acceptance metrics: schema-pass rate, token-drop incidents, and field-value drift vs FP32 baseline. Acceptance criteria for release gating: overall schema-pass rate >= 99.0% and critical-field failure delta <= 0.5% compared to FP32 on the canonical corpus.

Why this work: Function-calling is a critical integration surface for downstream apps. Quantization reduces cost but can change tokenization/next-token distribution and produce malformed structured output. A focused regression suite will give us signal to tune calibration, decide conservative fallback policies, and prevent customer-visible regressions.

Deliverables:
1) test corpus (s3://redwood-inference/quant-regressions/function-calls-v1) with tags for failure modes.
2) reproducible calibration job configs and logging (calib runs saved to artifact store).
3) CI job that runs quantized inference against the corpus and emits pass/fail + failure samples to a dashboard.
4) triage runbook documenting common failure signatures and mitigation steps.

Notes on calibration approach:
- Start with a 2k-sample calibration set sampled across short chat-style calls and long-form function-call prompts.
- Record per-layer activation histograms; prefer per-channel symmetric INT8 calibration for linear layers where supported.
- For FP8, evaluate both e4m3 and e5m2 encodings to spot systematic drift in logits for closing tokens that delimit JSON structures.
- If schema failures cluster around specific attention/kernel patterns, push for a targeted kernel selection or disable aggressive quant for those ops in production.

Metrics to capture per-run: schema_pass_rate, critical_field_pass_rate, median_latency, 95th_latency, token_error_rate, proportion_of_samples_requiring_fallback.

Acceptance criteria for promoting a quant profile to canary: must meet schema-pass gating above on canary traffic and show <= 3% cost increase regression when fallback is applied.

Integration points and stakeholders: runtime team (kernel selection), infra (CI/runner), QA (corpus review), PM (risk signoff), Console (dashboarding).
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha Malik created ticket. Initial scope reviewed with runtime and QA. Decided to prioritize function-call correctness over raw perf for first canary.

2026-02-24 - Spike: ran short calibration sweep on model-size-13B with e4m3 and INT8 symmetric. Observed ~1.8% schema failures for e4m3 vs baseline FP32 on 500-sample set. Logged histograms to s3://redwood-inference/quant-regressions/spike-20260224/.

2026-03-01 - Dataset: QA curated 2k prompts including deep nested object examples and streaming-edge cases. Corpus uploaded to s3://redwood-inference/quant-regressions/function-calls-v1 and linked in the description.

2026-03-03 - Decision: use ajv for JS-based validator in CI and python-jsonschema on the offline analysis path. Added semantic comparator to ignore benign whitespace/order differences for arrays when schema allows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-tests/pull/412

2026-03-06 - Calibration run results: e4m3 schema_pass_rate=98.7%, e5m2=99.1%, INT8=97.9% on the 2k corpus. Failures concentrated in long string truncation and missing closing braces when generation hit sequence length boundaries. Dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/quant/structured-output

2026-03-08 - Runtime feedback (Eliot Chen): some failures are correlated with KV-cache resizing on streaming requests. Proposed fix: ensure KV cache flushes happen before a function-call completion token is emitted or add delayed tokenization guard. Added as follow-up subtask ENG-18590.

2026-03-10 - PM review (Rita Gomez): requested explicit severity tagging for failures and a threshold for auto-fallback to FP32-hosted variant. Agreed to implement fallback when critical_field_pass_rate drops below 99.5% for any 100-sample window.

2026-03-12 - CI integration started. First gated job configured in GitHub Actions; will run quant-suite on every runtime-2.4 staging deploy. See workflow: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/blob/main/.github/workflows/quant-regress.yml

2026-03-14 - Latest: reran e5m2 with a small change to calibration sampling (stratified by prompt length). Schema_pass_rate improved to 99.35%. Moving to canary evaluation next week. Blocker: limited dedicated GPU capacity for prolonged canary runs; infra owner notified.
